ordered_diagnoses: Atrioventricular Block due to Lyme Disease

s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent syncope with transient complete atrioventricular block and ventricular asystole
salient_findings: Gradual slowing of the sinus rate and atrioventricular conduction
key_facts: Patient in their late 40s
No history of structural heart disease
No history of hypertension, myocarditis, or sleep apnea syndrome
No family history of cardiovascular disease and sudden death
Normal laboratory tests
Normal initial 12-lead ECG
Normal chest radiographic imaging
Normal echocardiographic findings
Holter monitor recording showed ventricular asystole during syncope
Electrophysiologic studies showed no abnormalities in the cardiac conduction system

shortlist: Atrioventricular Block due to Lyme Disease

shortlist.label: Sick Sinus Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient experienced ventricular asystole during syncope with gradual slowing of the sinus rate

shortlist.label: Carotid Sinus Hypersensitivity
shortlist.why_kept: Transient complete atrioventricular block and ventricular asystole suggest possible carotid sinus hypersensitivity

shortlist.label: Vasovagal Syncope
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent syncope with transient complete atrioventricular block and ventricular asystole could be related to vasovagal syncope

shortlist.label: Neurocardiogenic Syncope
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to vasovagal syncope, neurocardiogenic syncope could explain the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Atrioventricular Block due to Lyme Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, atrioventricular block due to Lyme disease is a possible cause of the patient's symptoms and should be considered

raw.rationale: The patient's Holter monitor recording showed a 23.8-second ventricular asystole during syncope, which is consistent with Sick Sinus Syndrome. The gradual slowing of the sinus rate and atrioventricular conduction followed by complete atrioventricular block also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Carotid Sinus Hypersensitivity
rejected.why: No evidence of carotid sinus massage or carotid sinus pressure leading to syncope

rejected.label: Vasovagal Syncope
rejected.why: No typical prodromal symptoms or triggers for vasovagal syncope

rejected.label: Neurocardiogenic Syncope
rejected.why: No evidence of neurocardiogenic causes, such as orthostatic hypotension or prolonged QT interval

rejected.label: Atrioventricular Block due to Lyme Disease
rejected.why: No evidence of Lyme disease or other infectious causes of atrioventricular block
